narrative.overview:
petitdoigt is the familiar quiet-dark typing test finished to the Linear / Raycast standard, with one change of unit: the finger, not the key, is what the screen teaches. One fixed screen holds three zones on a charcoal ground. The left rail carries the product's numbers, the centre stage drops falling notes straight onto an on-screen keyboard, and the right rail shows the hands with the finger to use filled in. Nothing scrolls on desktop and nothing needs a click to start; the primary action is typing.

The palette is restrained everywhere except where it carries meaning. Chrome stays in four steps of cool slate and three greys of text; color arrives only as finger hues in three row shades, one mustard accent for the product's own figures, and a coral for misses. Zones are separated by space and low-contrast hairlines rather than cards or boxes. Roboto Mono runs through everything, so legends, drill text and numerals share one grid and tabular digits never jump.

Motion is short and ease-out, with no bounce. The signature beat is a note landing on the strike line, its key cap pressing, and its finger lighting on the hands plate, all within about 80 to 220ms.
keyCharacteristics: One screen scaled from a 1536 x 1024 reference frame through the root font size.
Color is the finger; shape and shade are the row. That coding is the system's only chromatic language besides mustard and coral.
Flat charcoal surfaces; soft 8px key caps lit by a one-pixel top highlight.
Every control shares one hover / release / press timing.

rules.name: The Finger Means Finger Rule
rules.body: Pink, yellow, green, blue and the thumb grey mean a finger and nothing else. Never use them for status, category, decoration or charts that are not about fingers.

rules.name: The Row Shape Rule
rules.body: Shape and shade mean the row and nothing else. A mark for a key takes its row's shape, which points the way the finger travels from the home row: a triangle pointing up in the brighter shade for the top row, a circle in the plain hue for the home row, a triangle pointing down in the darker shade for the bottom row. The number row, when it is a target, is a diamond in the top-row shade; the space bar is a horizontal bar. A mark for a finger with no key in play (a stats-table finger marker, a result line) is that finger's home circle.

rules.name: The Second Channel Rule
rules.body: Color is never the only cue for the finger. A falling note sits in its finger's lane, a key cap sits in its finger's column, a matte fills the finger itself, and bars, tables and the next-key line spell the finger's name. The row is never shade alone either: shape always travels with it, and the next-key line spells the row.

rules.name: The One Brightness Rule
rules.body: In the stats view the keyboard's brightness means how much work a key needs, so the row shades switch off there and every key shows its home shade.

rules.name: The Mustard Is Ours Rule
rules.body: Mustard is for the wordmark and the figures the product measures. It is never a fill, never a button, never a finger.

rules.name: The Dim Fill, Never Dim Letter Rule
rules.body: Upcoming and finished tokens dim their fill (30% and 12% mixed toward Charcoal Ground) and switch their letter to light text, so the letter stays readable.

rules.name: The Lowercase Voice Rule
rules.body: Every visible string is lowercase, the wordmark included. No uppercase labels, no tracked small caps.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Roboto Mono for everything, numerals included; no second face.

rules.name: The No Boxes Rule
rules.body: Zones are separated by space and Hairline rules, never by cards, panels or bordered containers. Filled shapes are reserved for controls, key caps and finger tokens.

dos: Do size everything in rem from the 1536 x 1024 reference frame so the cockpit scales as one piece.
Do give every interactive element the shared interaction timing: 160ms hover in, 240ms release, 80ms press, 0.96 scale dip, ease-out `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`.
Do keep the reduced-motion override that collapses transitions and animations to near zero.
Do give every mark for a key its row's shape and shade: triangle up and brighter for the top row, circle and plain for the home row, triangle down and darker for the bottom row.
Do keep a second cue for the finger beside its color: the lane, the key column, the lit finger or the finger's name.
Do set text on a finger hue or on Miss Coral in Finger Ink.
Do separate zones with space and Hairline rules.
Do keep all copy lowercase and in Roboto Mono.
Do draw a history line in its subject's color: Mustard for the layout's own number, the finger's hue for a finger, the row's shade of it for a key.
Do write every string in both languages in src/core/i18n.ts, and look at the French at desktop and phone width before calling a screen done.
donts: Don't use a finger hue for anything that is not a finger: no status, category or link color, and no chart color except that finger's own history.
Don't use shape or shade for anything that is not the row, and never tie a shape to a finger.
Don't extend Mustard beyond the wordmark, the product's numbers and the few selection marks the build already carries.
Don't add a new yellow, or reuse Ring Yellow or Mustard for each other's role; the two values already sit too close and need separating rather than more overlap.
Don't wrap rails or drills in cards, panels or bordered boxes.
Don't introduce a second typeface or uppercase labels.
Don't use bounce, overshoot or spring easing.
